audits.title: Recognition session event contract, payload conversion, and minimum recording gate
notes: Recognition event reduction matches upstream: any Error event fails, the last FinalText wins, and Completed without Final/Error is a normal empty recognition rather than a backend failure.

Empty recognition returns an empty recognition payload, skips scene text postprocessing, and follows recording -> inferring -> idle without a postprocessing status; private D-Bus coverage proves the method reply and RecognitionResult carry the same empty payload.

Restored the upstream 8000 raw-sample minimum: shorter recordings cancel the session, return directly to idle, skip ASR/text finishing, and expose an exact empty StopRecording D-Bus reply without RecognitionResult.

Aligned streaming text projection so non-empty PartialText and early FinalText are emitted through RecognitionPartial during recording while early finals remain retained for stop-time payload construction and are not duplicated at stop.

Rust keeps a smaller typed BackendCapabilities shape because current upstream runtime decisions read only audio_delivery_mode; upstream supports_streaming, supports_partial_results, and requires_network are descriptor metadata without runtime consumers, while hotword capability is carried by model/provider metadata in both implementations.

The separate ERROR-INFO-001 audit now owns and implements frozen live RecognitionEvent::Error -> DaemonNotification classification; this recognition-contract unit remains non-overlapping and only owns event reduction/payload semantics.

audits.title: Recognition result JSON wire format and candidate source interpretation
notes: Daemon-produced raw/llm/asr recognition JSON, invalid-input fallback, commit-text normalization, and raw-candidate synthesis match the frozen upstream wire behavior.
Rust intentionally uses a typed CandidateSource: missing or unknown foreign source strings normalize to raw instead of preserving an arbitrary string; ordinary daemon-produced sources are unaffected.

Rust additionally preserves an empty cancel candidate and exposes RecognitionPayload::cancelled for typed frontend policy. The current Rust daemon does not produce that sentinel, and the frozen upstream defines kSourceCancel/menu handling but has no recognition-result producer for an empty cancel candidate.

audits.title: Core configuration schema, defaults, normalization, persistence, and validation
notes: Fixed dangling active ASR provider validation when the provider list is empty.
Validated input_gain in the upstream 0.1..10.0 range; Rust intentionally fails closed instead of clamping.
Rust scene provider omission remains an intentional extension because runtime provider resolution supports it.
Malformed/future-schema configs remain intentionally fail-closed.

audits.title: LLM command adapter process metadata and working-directory resolution
notes: Restored upstream args-first, command-second script-directory working-directory inference including ~/ expansion.
Explicit Rust working_dir remains a supported extension.
Fingerprint PID records, process groups, PID-reuse protection, and bounded TERM-to-KILL shutdown remain intentional safety enhancements.

audits.title: Scene/LLM post-processing, payload fallback, context, and OpenAI-compatible transport contract
notes: Aligned scoped vinput XML fallback tags, command fallback ordering, ASCII trimming, raw candidate retention, and recoverable LLM failure payloads.
Transport and prompt-file failures now preserve raw/selected+ASR payloads and emit typed warning notifications.
Context cache read failures are non-fatal like upstream.
OpenAI-compatible text connect attempts use the upstream 5-second maximum while scene timeout still bounds the full request.
Known gap: shutdown does not yet actively cancel an in-flight blocking OpenAI-compatible HTTP request; it waits for the request deadline.

audits.title: Prompt file loading and interpolation
notes: Unknown legacy double-brace placeholders remain verbatim.
Rust single-brace extensions no longer accidentally match double-brace legacy placeholders.

audits.title: Configured ASR backend selection and preparation
notes: Fixed local-provider dispatch to depend on type=local rather than the bundled sherpa-onnx provider id, matching upstream support for arbitrary stable local provider ids created by normal config/GUI flows.

Fixed local model backend selection so vinpst-model.json backend is authoritative exactly like upstream: missing/empty defaults offline, sherpa-offline selects offline, sherpa-streaming selects streaming, and unknown non-empty backend values fail closed; descriptive runtime metadata no longer overrides backend.
Command providers preserve the upstream id suffix rule: ids ending in .streaming use the streaming command backend and other command ids use batch mode.

Vinpst native OpenAI-compatible type=remote and the mock provider are intentional extensions beyond the frozen upstream factory; frozen upstream config variants are Local/Command and its browser remote service is a special command-provider path.

Rust build_active_prepared/prepare_backend consolidates warmup by creating and cancelling one session before swap. The corresponding upstream prepare/swap responsibility lives in recognition_session_manager and remains pending for its own non-overlapping audit.
Concrete model discovery/layout and native Sherpa implementation files are only supporting evidence here and remain pending for their dedicated model/backend audits.
Static configured ASR diagnostics now treat empty active_provider as a normal unselected state with empty last_error instead of reporting NoActiveProvider as a load failure.

audits.title: ASR session preparation, reload, and effective-backend state
notes: Fixed the valid empty active_provider state to match upstream disable semantics: startup and reload clear target/effective runtime ownership without treating the state as a backend-load failure, leave last_error empty, and future recording attempts fail only when a session is requested.

Reloading to an unselected provider while recording preserves the already-created active RecognitionSession but clears the effective backend for future sessions, matching upstream shared-backend session lifetime semantics.
Backend preparation still forces one CreateSession/cancel warmup before publication, matching upstream prepare-before-swap behavior.

Rust intentionally waits for Idle before preparing/applying a configured backend, whereas upstream can prepare/swap while a recording is active. This keeps runtime resource mutation outside busy recording/postprocessing phases.

Rust intentionally uses reload generations: stale prepared backends and stale failures are discarded, so an older request cannot be transiently published after a newer request arrives. Frozen upstream may briefly apply the earlier prepared backend before processing the later request.

Rust intentionally does not use the upstream BuildRuntimeSignature no-op optimization. Explicit reload requests therefore re-prepare even for apparently unchanged identity, which also avoids missing changes such as VAD thresholds/durations that the upstream signature does not include.
Reload success is silent and reload failure emits one notification in both implementations. Rust additionally suppresses stale-generation failure notifications.

Process-level --no-asr remains sticky across config reloads in both implementations. Rust intentionally exposes its disable reason through typed/D-Bus diagnostics; frozen upstream only reports that reason to stderr and leaves snapshot last_error empty.

Frozen upstream session snapshots use ResolvePreferredLocalModel even for non-local active providers, while Rust diagnostics report the active Command/Remote provider model. Exact legacy D-Bus state projection is deferred to the separate common/dbus ASR-state audit because the Rust projection file remains pending.

Upstream explicitly joins its reload thread during Shutdown. Rust owns reload work in Tokio tasks; async workers are cancelled with runtime shutdown while spawn_blocking preparation is waited by Tokio runtime teardown. No detached native preparation is intentionally created.

audits.title: Command ASR batch and streaming process protocols
notes: Fixed the main streaming gap: .streaming command providers now own one long-lived helper process across PushAudio calls instead of buffering all PCM until Finish. Intermediate chunks are sent with commit=false, the final pending chunk uses commit=true, and a finish control line closes input exactly like frozen upstream.

The daemon live poller now actively polls asynchronous streaming sessions on every tick, so helper stdout produced after PushAudio returns can reach RecognitionPartial before StopRecording. Early FinalText remains retained for the final payload and is not duplicated at stop.

Streaming JSON event handling matches upstream for session_started/empty/unknown no-ops, trimmed partial/final/final_timestamps text, duplicate-partial suppression, blank error fallback, closed completion, and malformed JSON fail-closed behavior.

Streaming cancel best-effort starts the helper, sends a cancel control event, emits Completed, and terminates the helper process group; tests prove descendant cleanup. Buffered command cancel now also emits Completed and buffered Finish is idempotent like upstream.

Batch command providers continue to write raw signed-16 little-endian PCM and use trimmed stdout as final text. On supported little-endian Linux targets this matches upstream native i16 byte transport.

Vinpst intentionally retains stronger process safety than frozen upstream: command helpers run in their own process group, direct-child exit cleans descendants, and stdout/stderr are independently capped at 1 MiB. Frozen upstream batch/streaming collectors have no comparable output cap and do not isolate a process group.

Frozen upstream streaming ignores provider timeout_ms and uses a fixed 10 second final wait with unbounded recording-stage pipe waits. Vinpst uses the same 10 second default when timeout_ms is absent, but an explicitly configured timeout bounds each streaming pipe write and final wait without imposing one whole-session deadline, so long recordings are not killed merely because their duration exceeds the provider timeout.

Existing Vinpst batch/JSON one-shot semantics intentionally keep timeout_ms=None as no configured deadline; managed provider materialization supplies 60000 ms. Frozen upstream leaves an omitted timeout at integer zero, which can immediately expire its batch helper deadline. This pre-existing safer behavior is preserved rather than copying the zero-timeout edge case.

The former one-shot LegacyCommandStreamingRunner is now test-only protocol coverage; production factory wiring uses LegacyCommandStreamingBackend. The .streaming suffix remains the authoritative selector and registry validation already requires stream metadata to agree with that suffix.
Live RecognitionEvent::Error -> DaemonNotification classification is now completed by the separate ERROR-INFO-001 audit; this command unit continues to own helper protocol/process semantics only.

audits.title: Native Sherpa offline and streaming recognition runtime
notes: Fixed native PCM scaling to divide signed i16 samples by 32768.0 for both offline and online recognizers, matching frozen upstream full-scale normalization.

Fixed native session lifecycle parity: repeated Finish is idempotent, Cancel is idempotent and yields Completed, and a completed recognizer with no text is a normal empty recognition rather than a backend error.
Restored upstream result extraction fallback: non-empty result.text wins; otherwise concatenated result.tokens are trimmed and used for offline results, online partials/endpoints, and final results.

Fixed online endpoint behavior: after each decode step, endpoint detection emits any changed hypothesis before resetting the stream, then decoding continues. Endpoint reset does not invent an application-level final/commit; push-to-talk still finalizes on StopRecording.
Fixed stop-time online projection so a final hypothesis that differs from the last emitted partial is first emitted as PartialText and then FinalText, exactly matching frozen upstream.

Model hotwords are now gated by top-level supports_hotwords. Provider hotwords override model hotwords, unsupported models ignore them at runtime, and an effective hotword path forces modified_beam_search for both offline and online recognizers.

Added all frozen-upstream online families supported by the sherpa-onnx Rust binding: transducer, zipformer2_ctc, paraformer, nemo_ctc, and t_one_ctc, with path-level metadata tests and native-feature compilation.

Aligned thread policy: offline metadata defaults to 4 threads when omitted while explicit offline model metadata may override it; online runtime uses the frozen upstream runtime default of 4 threads rather than model metadata.
All frozen offline family mappings are now owned and completed by ASR-MODEL-001; this runtime unit retains only recognizer/session behavior ownership.

Known gap: frozen upstream can supply model tokens and hotwords through in-memory tokens_buf/hotwords_buf JSON byte strings. The later model-manager audit verified that sherpa-onnx 1.13.3 safe high-level OfflineModelConfig/OnlineModelConfig does not expose those C-API fields, so Vinpst keeps the gap explicit rather than adding raw unsafe FFI.
Model path discovery/layout inference and VAD remain supporting evidence only and stay pending for their own non-overlapping audits.

audits.title: Offline Silero VAD trimming
notes: Silero detector construction matches frozen upstream: 16 kHz, 512-sample window, threshold/min-speech/min-silence controls, max speech duration 0, one CPU thread, debug disabled, and a 30 second detector buffer.

VAD config defaults are exactly aligned at enabled=true, threshold=0.45, min_speech_duration=0.15, min_silence_duration=0.5, and speech_pad_ms=300; config-level and resolved-plan tests pin the mapping so the two duration fields cannot be swapped.

Trim behavior matches upstream for reset, exact 512-sample feeds, zero-padding the final partial window, flush, segment extraction, independent per-segment speech padding, concatenation including overlapping padded regions, and returning original audio when no speech is found.

VAD model resolution intentionally differs from the frozen compile-time VINPUT_VAD_MODEL_PATH: Vinpst supports an explicit VINPST_SHERPA_VAD_MODEL, user/system XDG data locations, and a development asset. Missing/unloadable VAD still fails open to untrimmed audio like upstream.

Vinpst intentionally adds a 500 ms cold-start guard for the first detected segment: if its padded start lies within the first 500 ms, trimming preserves audio from sample zero to reduce first-syllable clipping after capture startup. Frozen vad_trimmer.cpp has no equivalent guard.

Frozen upstream initializes the detector at 16 kHz and ignores the sample_rate argument passed to Trim. Vinpst production capture is likewise 16 kHz, but injected/non-16-kHz PCM explicitly bypasses VAD instead of running a 16-kHz detector against mismatched-rate samples.
VAD remains offline/buffered only in both implementations; online/streaming Sherpa recognition does not use this trimmer.

audits.title: Installed ASR model discovery, metadata, layout, and removal
notes: Audited frozen installed-model discovery, metadata/path validation, runtime-language hints, model validation/removal safety, and native Sherpa family asset mapping without absorbing live registry network/schema ownership.

Fixed metadata path containment for offline and online Sherpa assets, including parent and symlink escapes; managed removal now rejects symlink targets and verifies canonical root containment while retaining Vinpst active-model protection.

Fixed native model coverage and metadata semantics: all 19 frozen offline families and all five frozen streaming families are accepted, including nemo_transducer family-keyed assets, Moonshine v2 encoder+merged-decoder layouts, frozen Qwen3/FunASR defaults, Whisper timestamp flags, and frozen RuntimeLanguageHint behavior.

Installed discovery now preserves malformed metadata entries as explicit broken models instead of failing the whole catalog; CLI reports broken state, daemon target menus exclude broken models, and GUI semantic state disables Use while keeping removal available.
Intentional Vinpst extensions remain: flat managed-model discovery in addition to the frozen two-level layout, a moonshine_v1 compatibility alias, and stronger active-model/symlink removal guards.

Remaining dependency gap: frozen tokens_buf/hotwords_buf in-memory Sherpa metadata cannot be represented through sherpa-onnx 1.13.3 safe Rust Offline/Online model configs; normal crates remain unsafe-free rather than bypassing the binding with raw FFI.

audits.title: Daemon error classification and notification payloads
notes: Ported the frozen daemon ClassifyErrorText taxonomy into one crate-private classifier preserving code, subject, detail, raw-message, prefix recursion, nested provider/model adoption, model/audio/D-Bus failures, LLM/HTTP processing failures, prompt-file URI parsing, and unknown fallback.

D-Bus emission now uses the classifier for recording-start failures, live streaming RecognitionEvent::Error, stop-time ASR failures, text postprocess failures, and current-generation ASR reload failures. Live Error events are drained in event order while the session retains its fatal state, so Stop produces no fabricated text and does not duplicate an already-emitted notification.

Private-session D-Bus evidence proves exact daemon_busy and asr_provider_timeout ssss payloads, live notification before Stop, stop-time notification before the operation failure, and bounded no-duplicate behavior. The complete daemon lib suite and 19 private-bus integration tests pass under strict dbus-integration Clippy.

The frozen header also defines daemon_start_failed and daemon_restart_failed, but frozen generation occurs only in cli/runtime/systemd_client.{cpp,h}, not error_info.cpp. The corresponding Rust CLI daemon-control files remain pending and do not yet project those two structured codes; that cross-module gap stays assigned to the later CLI-service audit rather than creating unused daemon constants.

audits.title: Legacy D-Bus names, status values, and ASR backend state classification
notes: Audited the frozen daemon service/notifier names, five wire status values, OperationFailed class, eight-field AsrBackendState shape, and requested-backend classification. The eight frozen daemon service methods and four signals remain present with the same member names; Notify is correctly kept on the separate frontend-notifier interface rather than the daemon service list.
Vinpst intentionally applies its independent product namespace to bus/object/interface/error/notifier identities and exposes additional daemon extension methods. No Vinput aliases are added.

Added ServiceStatus::parse_legacy_wire to reproduce frozen StringToStatus unknown->idle behavior while preserving the existing strict parse_wire API for Rust consumers so protocol drift remains fail-closed internally.

Requested ASR backend classification matches frozen precedence and exact provider/model equality. The eight state fields also match. Runtime projection intentionally differs for command/remote providers: Vinpst reports the model on the actual target/effective provider, while frozen ResolvePreferredLocalModel can report an unrelated active/first local model; the richer Vinpst diagnostic is retained.

Remote endpoints remain part of the frozen AsrBackendState shape. Vinpst fills them from the selected remote provider with diagnostic URL redaction; this is compatible with the field contract and more explicit than an empty-only projection.

audits.title: Daemon D-Bus method dispatch and signal emission
notes: Audited all eight frozen method handlers and four daemon signals against the Rust service facade. Legacy methods dispatch to the corresponding runtime or adapter operation and failures retain the Vinpst OperationFailed error class; runtime/controller state-machine semantics remain owned by later non-overlapping units.

Vinpst intentionally serializes recording transactions and completes inference/postprocessing before StopRecording returns the finalized JSON payload. Frozen upstream accepts StopRecording, returns an empty string immediately, and delivers the eventual result only by signal. The synchronous Rust contract is documented architecture, prevents stop/start overlap, and is consumed by the retained Rust Fcitx/CLI clients.

Session-bus ownership intentionally differs: frozen upstream requests replace-existing/allow-replacement, while Vinpst uses DoNotQueue so a second daemon cannot replace or queue behind the current owner. Private session-bus coverage pins the single-owner behavior.

Vinpst intentionally normalizes, credential-redacts, and bounds OperationFailed descriptions before exposing runtime errors on D-Bus instead of forwarding the frozen raw message verbatim. Focused coverage pins Authorization/Bearer redaction, whitespace normalization, and the Unicode-safe 512-character bound.

Frozen worker-thread signal forwarding uses an eventfd-backed queue into the bus thread. Rust uses zbus async signal emission from serialized service/runtime transitions and a generation-cancelled live-partial poller; private-bus integration coverage exercises recognition result/partial, status, notification, adapter, and reload paths without retaining the C++ queue mechanism.

Service lifetime is expressed through the held zbus Connection and Rust ownership rather than explicit Start/Stop bus methods: RuntimeState Drop restores output state, cancels capture/active recognition, and stops managed adapters, while the daemon explicitly shuts down its remote text service before releasing the service.

audits.title: Recognition result post-processing dispatch and status transition
notes: Fixed a user-visible status gap in the Rust-fused stop pipeline: non-empty recognized text no longer implies Postprocessing. Text-processor invocation and the postprocessing status transition are now separate decisions, matching the frozen recognition pipeline.

Normal scenes enter Postprocessing only when recognized text is non-empty, candidate_count is positive, provider_id is non-empty, and prompt is non-empty. Command scenes use the frozen command rule: recognized text, positive candidate_count, and a non-empty provider are sufficient; the command prompt is not an additional status gate.

Raw scenes, command paths without a configured processor provider, and adapter/no-provider scenes remain Inferring while the typed text processor still constructs the final payload. Focused runtime coverage and the private session-bus suite pin those negative cases, while a provider+prompt+candidate LLM scene pins the positive recording -> inferring -> postprocessing -> idle sequence.

Empty recognition already follows the frozen early-return behavior under ASR-CONTRACT-001. Final payload construction and text-provider/adapter semantics remain owned by the existing TXT-* units, while structured notification classification remains owned by ERROR-INFO-001.

Frozen RecognitionPipeline can report a null PostProcessor as a runtime error. Rust intentionally makes that state unrepresentable: RuntimeState owns a Box<dyn TextProcessor> at construction, so recognition cannot enter the pipeline without a processor object.

Frozen debug mode logs recognized text, truncated after 2048 bytes. Vinpst intentionally does not copy that diagnostic because its architecture contract forbids structured tracing from including recognized text; timing and target metadata remain sufficient for runtime diagnostics without retaining user dictation content.
The controller's worker scheduling, capture lifetime, status callbacks, and stop/reload state-machine ownership remain pending in DAEMON-CONTROLLER-001 and are not duplicated here.

audits.title: Daemon recording controller state machine and active-session orchestration
notes: Fixed controller-level buffered preprocessing to follow the frozen audio algebra instead of the earlier generic Rust helper: fixed silence-threshold trimming is no longer injected at this layer, i16 gain uses clamp plus truncation toward zero, and normalize_audio only amplifies a non-silent peak below 0.1 to full scale without attenuating louder audio. Silero VAD remains owned by ASR-VAD-001 rather than being duplicated in the controller.

Vinpst intentionally applies configured input_gain to both buffered and streaming sessions. Frozen streaming delivery applies the gain, but frozen buffered StopRecording overwrites its gain-adjusted callback buffer with raw StopAndGetBuffer PCM before inference and therefore drops the gain. That contradicts the frozen GUI/config contract describing input gain as a microphone multiplier applied to captured audio; Vinpst retains the user-facing contract rather than reproducing that upstream buffered-path bug.

Fixed live streaming PushAudio failures to become observable immediately instead of being deferred until StopRecording: the next live poll enters Error, disables capture callbacks, cancels the active recognition session/capture, restores output, emits error status plus the raw daemon notification, then recovers to Idle. Runtime and private-session D-Bus coverage prove this path without requiring a StopRecording call. RecognitionEvent::Error remains the separate frozen behavior owned by ERROR-INFO-001: it emits a classified notification while recording and is not promoted to the controller Error phase.

Start/rollback ordering is aligned and pinned: capture begins before RecognitionSession creation; session-creation failure cancels already-started capture and returns Idle; successful setup then exposes Recording and output ducking. Rust additionally gates early recorder callbacks until the session is installed and replays them in order, avoiding a frozen-style start-window race without changing delivered PCM order.

Streaming delivery matches the frozen controller's 800-sample chunk size, applies gain before each push, and flushes one final short tail without replaying already-delivered samples. Buffered and streaming paths both retain the frozen 8000 raw-sample minimum recording gate before ASR finishing.

Stop/reload/shutdown ownership is intentionally split rather than duplicated: Vinpst's serialized synchronous StopRecording transaction is recorded under DBUS-SERVICE-001, backend preparation/generation semantics under ASR-SESSION-001, and output-ducker/capture internals remain pending dedicated audio units. Reset-to-idle still applies a deferred reload, and RuntimeState Drop disables callbacks, cancels active recognition/capture, restores output, and cleans up supervised adapters.

Frozen eventfd notification, deferred capture-stop queue, start_recording_in_progress flag, and native worker thread primarily serialize races created by its callback/thread model. Vinpst intentionally uses the D-Bus recording transaction lock, Rust ownership/RAII, the capture-start gate, and async task cancellation instead of recreating those mechanisms. The frozen timing-only debug markers for recording start, first non-silent chunk, and first partial are not required product behavior and are not copied into user-content-safe tracing.

Recognition postprocessing remains owned by RECOGNITION-PIPELINE-001; audio capture implementation and output-ducker internals remain separate pending units, so this controller audit does not claim those files by supporting reference.

audits.title: Default output sink ducking and restoration
notes: Audited frozen wpctl behavior end to end: both implementations use @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@, a 2000 ms command deadline, current_volume * clamped_scale, four-decimal set-volume arguments, successful-set-before-saving semantics, idempotent repeated Duck, and one-shot Restore that clears saved state even if restoration fails.

Fixed a Rust process-supervision gap by replacing the output-ducker's private poll/spawn/read loop with the shared vinpst-process supervisor. The deadline now covers output recovery, stdout/stderr are bounded, and the direct child plus inherited descendants are reaped as one process group. Focused coverage proves both an ordinary timeout and the former parent-exit/descendant-held-output-pipe hang case.

Vinpst intentionally parses wpctl output more strictly than frozen strtod: non-finite and negative volumes are rejected, and the numeric token must parse completely. set-volume likewise rejects non-finite/negative values. Normal plain and [MUTED] wpctl output remains compatible; the stricter behavior is fail-closed for malformed external output.

Frozen OutputDucker uses an internal mutex because it may be called across its native controller threads. Rust requires mutable ownership of OutputDucker and serializes controller transitions instead, so reproducing the mutex would add no product behavior. Logging is routed through tracing rather than frozen stderr/debug helpers.

Controller-level duck/restore call ordering and shutdown restoration are already owned and covered by DAEMON-CONTROLLER-001; this unit only owns the volume-control implementation and process boundary.

audits.title: PipeWire capture lifecycle, target binding, and reusable stream policy
notes: Aligned the live PipeWire stream contract with frozen AudioCapture: S16LE at 16 kHz mono, Audio/Capture/Communication properties, stream.capture.sink=false so autoconnect targets sources rather than sink output, optional target.object for explicit sources, and AUTOCONNECT|INACTIVE|MAP_BUFFERS stream flags.

Removed Vinpst's extra RT_PROCESS request. The frozen capture stream does not request realtime process callbacks, while the Rust process path allocates a chunk Vec, extends the accumulated buffer, locks the callback holder, and may invoke a user callback; advertising that callback as RT-process-safe was both unnecessary for parity and a poor fit for its actual work.

Fixed reusable-stream fallback cleanup: when set_active(true) fails on a reused stream, Rust now drops the failed stream before creating the replacement, matching frozen DestroyStream-before-recreate semantics. A failed replacement therefore cannot leave the known-bad stream cached for another retry.

Reusable stream policy otherwise matches: reuse defaults on, explicit false-like opt-outs disable it, idle destroy defaults to 15000 ms and caps at 600000 ms, target/PCM mismatch forces recreation, successful stop deactivates and preserves the stream, and failed deactivation destroys it. Rust uses a generation-guarded timer worker instead of frozen daemon-main-loop polling for idle expiration; stale timers cannot destroy a new recording.

PCM delivery matches the frozen process callback: malformed/empty buffers are ignored, byte bounds are checked, odd trailing bytes are ignored, every accepted i16 sample is appended to the stop buffer and also forwarded to the installed chunk callback, and first-buffer latency is recorded once per recording. Rust copies PipeWire bytes into owned little-endian samples before callback delivery instead of exposing the mapped PipeWire buffer span directly.

Stop/cancel/drop semantics are equivalent at the product boundary: normal stop returns accumulated audio and either leaves a bounded inactive reusable stream or tears the worker down; cancellation discards the recording and destroys reusable state; Drop shuts down the worker and stream. Rust's dedicated worker owns its PipeWire main loop/context, whereas frozen AudioCapture keeps one pw_thread_loop for object lifetime.

Vinpst intentionally keeps independent environment names (VINPST_CAPTURE_REUSE / VINPST_CAPTURE_IDLE_DESTROY_MS), stream/client identity, and typed capture targets. Empty capture targets are rejected by typed config instead of being a second spelling of frozen default; the canonical user value is default. Idle target changes are lazily invalidated at the next Begin through config mismatch rather than immediately destroying the inactive stream, but the next recording cannot reuse the old target.

Frozen onParamChanged only prints the negotiated format; it does not reject a negotiated mismatch. Vinpst does not reproduce that stderr-only diagnostic. Device discovery code shares the Rust source file but remains pending for the separate common/audio/pipewire_device audit, and controller preprocessing/call ordering remains owned by DAEMON-CONTROLLER-001.

audits.title: PipeWire audio-source discovery and enumeration failure semantics
notes: Frozen and Rust discovery agree on the core registry contract: only PipeWire Node globals with media.class=Audio/Source are returned, registry arrival order is preserved, the registry object id is retained, and missing node.name/node.description values become empty strings. A direct run of both compiled CLIs against the live user PipeWire session returned the same two sources in the same 69 -> 55 order.

The one-shot synchronization model is equivalent: both attach the registry listener before issuing a core sync and stop the main loop only when the matching core done sequence arrives. Rust relies on pipewire-rs RAII for registry/core/context/main-loop cleanup instead of explicit destroy/disconnect calls.

Vinpst intentionally does not reproduce frozen failure ambiguity. Frozen EnumerateAudioSources returns an empty vector for main-loop/context/core setup failure, so its CLI cannot distinguish no microphones from PipeWire being unavailable. Rust returns AudioError::DeviceEnumerationFailed; CLI/daemon diagnostics degrade that to devices=[] plus live=false and enumeration_error while still exiting successfully, and the GUI surfaces a retryable microphone-refresh failure. Direct compiled-binary comparison with PIPEWIRE_REMOTE pointing at a missing server confirms this distinction.

Vinpst also keeps process-global pipewire-rs initialization instead of frozen per-call pw_init/pw_deinit. pipewire-rs guards pw_init with OnceLock, avoiding repeated global initialization/deinitialization when CLI/GUI discovery is invoked more than once or from independent product surfaces.

The Rust text device list deliberately retains the canonical default capture target even when live discovery fails, whereas frozen device list exits after its ambiguous empty-result message before printing default. This is consistent with Vinpst typed config: default remains a valid selection independent of whether live enumeration is currently available.

The shared Rust implementation file remains owned by AUDIO-CAPTURE-001 and is supporting evidence here. Device-list/use CLI command semantics beyond enumeration, and standalone-GUI presentation behavior beyond consuming the enumerator result, remain owned by their pending CLI/GUI audit units.

audits.title: Audio gain and quiet peak-normalization algebra
notes: Fixed the shared Rust i16 gain helper to match frozen ApplyGainI16 exactly at the sample boundary: multiply in f32, clamp to [-32768, 32767], then truncate toward zero. The previous generic helper rounded first, which could differ by one LSB; daemon buffered and streaming delivery now delegate to the corrected vinpst-audio implementation instead of maintaining duplicate controller math.

Moved frozen default PeakNormalize algebra into PcmBuffer::normalize_quiet_to_full_scale and made the controller delegate to it. Non-zero peaks below 0.1 full scale are amplified to full scale, peaks at or above the threshold are never attenuated, and zero audio is unchanged. Deterministic tests cover quiet/loud/silent cases and the exact i16 threshold boundary where 3276 is below 0.1 but 3277 is above it.

Removed the pre-parity AudioProcessingOptions abstraction plus its generic target-normalization and fixed-threshold silence-trimming helpers. Repository-wide search found no production consumer; the abstraction encoded the obsolete trim -> normalize -> gain order and its architecture documentation contradicted the audited runtime contract. Silence trimming remains owned by the separate Silero VAD backend rather than a fixed PCM threshold.

Updated the audio architecture contract to the actual product path: input gain is applied at capture delivery, buffered sessions optionally perform quiet-only peak normalization after gain, and this layer performs no fixed-threshold trim. Earlier prose claiming trim/normalize/gain was the buffered backend contract was stale scaffold documentation.

Frozen ApplyGain(float) has no caller and Rust has no product float-PCM processing surface, so Vinpst intentionally does not reproduce that dead generic helper. Frozen PeakNormalize's custom target_peak/low_threshold parameters are likewise unused; Rust exposes only the default production behavior instead of widening the public API for unexercised knobs.

Vinpst keeps its existing fail-closed handling for non-finite gain values: PcmBuffer leaves audio unchanged, while typed configuration rejects non-finite/out-of-range input_gain before runtime. Frozen product configuration also constrains gain, so this hardening does not change valid user behavior. The separate buffered-input-gain divergence caused by frozen StopAndGetBuffer overwrite remains documented under DAEMON-CONTROLLER-001.
